core_obligations: Prove the two statements (proof lines 808-827). Part (1): morphisms-lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change (tag 02FY) gives a point x' of X' mapping to x with trdeg_{kappa(f'(x'))}(kappa(x')) = r (proof lines 809-810). Part (2): given x'_1, x'_2 as in (1), since X'' = X' x_X X' the cited Descent lemma (tag 02KI) produces x'' in X'' mapping to both x'_1 and x'_2 (proof lines 811-814); let s'' in S'', s'_i in S', s in S be the images of x'', x'_i, x, let k = kappa(s), and let Z be the integral closed subscheme of X_k whose generic point is x; then each x'_i is a generic point of an irreducible component of Z_{kappa(s'_i)} (proof lines 815-819); choose an irreducible component Z'' of Z_{kappa(s'')} containing x'' with generic point xi''; since xi'' specializes to x'' the two projections map xi'' to x'_i (proof lines 820-823), and trdeg_{kappa(s'')}(kappa(xi'')) = r because xi'' is a generic point of an irreducible component of the base change of Z (proof lines 824-826).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) by the cited dimension-of-fibres lemma (proof lines 809-810).
Existence of a common point x'' over both x'_i via the fibre product X'' = X' x_X X' (proof lines 811-814).
Integral closed subscheme Z and the generic point xi'' of the component containing x'' force both projections and give trdeg r (proof lines 815-826).
